canonicalDefinition: Moolank 1 tradition may associate this number with visible contribution, respect and acknowledgment. In a balanced expression, recognition is valued as fair credit and useful feedback while motivation, cooperation and self-worth remain stable without constant praise. Under pressure, especially when contribution feels ignored or status feels reduced, the same sensitivity may become visibility competition, resentment, disproportionate credit-taking or dependence on approval. This is a secondary, lower-confidence traditional tendency rather than a universal trait.

corePattern.trigger: A situation involving acknowledgment, public credit, visibility, rank or evaluation
corePattern.internalResponse: Heightened attention to whether contribution and standing are being recognized fairly
corePattern.behaviour: Seeks clear attribution, respectful acknowledgment or visible ownership
corePattern.possibleConsequence: Constructive clarification and shared credit when balanced; resentment, status competition or disproportionate credit claims when threatened

traitBoundaries.confidence: Confidence concerns perceived capability; recognition sensitivity concerns response to acknowledgment and public evaluation.
traitBoundaries.selfEsteem: Valuing fair credit does not prove fragile self-esteem. Personal worth must not be made contingent on praise, rank or visibility.
traitBoundaries.ambition: Ambition concerns achievement or advancement. Recognition may accompany ambition but does not define it.
traitBoundaries.dominance: Seeking fair credit does not justify controlling others, suppressing dissent or claiming superior decision rights.
traitBoundaries.entitlement: Entitlement assumes special treatment regardless of contribution or agreement; healthy recognition sensitivity asks for proportionate credit.
traitBoundaries.praiseDependence: Recognition may matter without motivation or self-worth depending on repeated approval.
traitBoundaries.socialComparison: Comparison may trigger recognition concerns but is not the same construct.
traitBoundaries.leadership: Effective leadership requires sharing credit, recognizing invisible work and tolerating dissent.
traitBoundaries.disrespect: Absent praise, disagreement or lower visibility do not automatically equal disrespect. Context and agreements matter.

appCard.strength: Values fair acknowledgment and accurate credit for contribution.
appCard.shadow: May compete for visibility or feel overlooked when credit and status seem unclear.
appCard.growthKey: Clarify ownership, share credit and keep self-worth separate from praise, title and visibility.

appSafeSummary: Moolank 1 tradition may associate you with valuing visible contribution, fair credit and respectful acknowledgment. This tendency is most useful when recognition works as feedback rather than proof of worth. When ownership or status feels unclear, pause before assuming disrespect, clarify attribution directly and recognize shared or invisible work. Direct traditional support for this specific tendency is limited, so it should be read as a possibility rather than a fixed trait.
